descVi: Giao tiếp công sở, phỏng vấn, thăng tiến và môi trường làm việc.

words.definitionEn: To give someone a task, role, or resource
words.exampleDailyEn: The coach assigned each player a partner for practice.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers should assign tasks that match students' abilities while encouraging them to develop new skills.

words.definitionEn: To help someone do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: A friendly librarian assisted me with the printer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local volunteers can assist older residents with online services, making essential information more accessible.

words.definitionEn: Having the ability or qualities needed to do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: This little printer is capable of producing excellent colour photos.
words.exampleIeltsEn: With appropriate training and support, young employees are capable of taking on substantial responsibilities within an organisation.

words.definitionEn: A strong willingness to give time and effort to something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her commitment to gardening keeps the flowers blooming.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improving public transport requires sustained political commitment and reliable funding rather than occasional investment in isolated projects.

words.definitionEn: willing to help others or work together
words.exampleDailyEn: Everyone was cooperative when we rearranged the shared kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cooperative learning can help students develop communication skills while taking shared responsibility for completing a task.

words.definitionEn: A legally established company, especially a large one.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister works for a corporation that makes furniture.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A multinational corporation can create local jobs, but its profits may largely flow back to overseas shareholders.

words.definitionEn: Full of energy and eager to make things happen.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our dynamic coach keeps everyone moving throughout the session.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A dynamic economy requires businesses to adapt quickly to technological advances and changing consumer preferences.

words.definitionEn: Specialist knowledge or skills gained through training and experience.
words.exampleDailyEn: We need your expertise to repair this old clock.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities can support local businesses by sharing their expertise in renewable energy and sustainable manufacturing.

words.definitionEn: the ability to change or adapt to different needs
words.exampleDailyEn: This job gives me flexibility to collect my daughter.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Greater flexibility in working hours can help employees balance professional responsibilities with family commitments.

words.definitionEn: to establish an organization, institution, or settlement
words.exampleDailyEn: My aunt founded a small charity last winter.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Graduates who found new businesses can create employment opportunities and introduce innovative services to local communities.

words.definitionEn: To examine something carefully for faults or other details.
words.exampleDailyEn: Please inspect the bicycle's brakes before you ride it.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should inspect rental properties regularly to ensure that tenants have safe and healthy living conditions.

words.definitionEn: work, especially physical work, or the workers who perform it
words.exampleDailyEn: Repairing the old fence took a full day of labor.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investment in automation can reduce labor costs, but governments must help displaced workers develop new skills.

words.definitionEn: To get something, especially through effort or a formal process.
words.exampleDailyEn: You can obtain a replacement key from the landlord.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers must obtain informed consent from participants before collecting personal data for a scientific study.

words.definitionEn: existing or happening before something else
words.exampleDailyEn: You need prior permission to use this room.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Applicants with prior experience in community work may adapt more quickly to roles in public services.

words.definitionEn: Continue an activity or move to its next stage.
words.exampleDailyEn: We can proceed with dinner once everyone arrives.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should consult residents before they proceed with major changes to public transport.

words.definitionEn: The possibility or expectation that something will happen.
words.exampleDailyEn: The prospect of a beach holiday cheered us up.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to vocational training can improve employment prospects for young people in economically disadvantaged regions.

words.definitionEn: To refuse to accept, approve, or believe something.
words.exampleDailyEn: The shop rejected my offer for the old bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may reject construction proposals if developers cannot demonstrate that nearby wildlife habitats will be protected.

words.definitionEn: keep or continue to have something
words.exampleDailyEn: This old house still retains its original wooden doors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Flexible working arrangements can help companies retain experienced employees while improving overall job satisfaction.

words.definitionEn: To try to find or obtain something.
words.exampleDailyEn: You should seek advice before buying a used car.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many graduates seek employment abroad to gain professional experience and develop their language skills.

words.definitionEn: To state exactly what is required or meant.
words.exampleDailyEn: Please specify which colour you want for the curtains.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should specify clear safety standards that all manufacturers must meet before selling products to consumers.

words.definitionEn: The work of organising and running an institution or business.
words.exampleDailyEn: She handles the administration for our local sports club.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Efficient administration allows public hospitals to allocate resources fairly and respond more quickly to patients' needs.

words.definitionEn: Related to organising and running an institution or business.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister handles administrative tasks at a local clinic.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Reducing administrative costs could allow schools to spend more money on teaching materials and student support.

words.definitionEn: a meeting or explanation giving essential information or instructions
words.exampleDailyEn: Our guide gave us a briefing before the hike.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A clear safety briefing helps construction workers understand potential hazards before they begin unfamiliar tasks.

words.definitionEn: A separate condition or requirement in a legal document.
words.exampleDailyEn: One clause in our lease allows us to keep pets.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employment contracts should include a clause that clearly defines workers' rights to paid leave and flexible working.

words.definitionEn: An expert paid to provide specialist advice.
words.exampleDailyEn: We hired a consultant to help improve our small business.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An environmental consultant can help companies reduce waste while ensuring that their operations comply with national regulations.

words.definitionEn: A legally binding agreement between people or organisations.
words.exampleDailyEn: Read the contract carefully before you agree to sign it.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A clear employment contract protects both workers and employers by defining responsibilities, working hours and payment terms.

words.definitionEn: working together or helping by doing what is requested
words.exampleDailyEn: The neighbours are cooperating to repair the shared fence.
words.exampleIeltsEn: By cooperating on clean energy research, countries can reduce costs and accelerate the development of sustainable technologies.

words.definitionEn: Organising people or activities so they work effectively together
words.exampleDailyEn: Moving this sofa upstairs will take some coordination.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Effective coordination between schools and health services can improve support for children with additional needs.

words.definitionEn: Relating to a company or businesses in general.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister handles corporate travel for a small company.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Greater corporate transparency allows consumers to assess whether businesses genuinely meet their environmental and social commitments.

words.definitionEn: To give time, effort, or resources to someone or something.
words.exampleDailyEn: I devote an hour each evening to practising the piano.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should devote more resources to preventive healthcare rather than relying entirely on expensive medical treatments.

words.definitionEn: an early version of writing that may be changed
words.exampleDailyEn: I saved the first draft of my letter.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should publish draft legislation early so that citizens can comment before final decisions are made.

words.definitionEn: able to change to suit different needs or situations
words.exampleDailyEn: My flexible schedule lets me collect the children after school.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Flexible working arrangements can help employees balance professional responsibilities with their family commitments.

words.definitionEn: Advice or a principle explaining how something should be done.
words.exampleDailyEn: These guidelines explain how to store food safely.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Clear guidelines on data collection can help researchers protect participants while maintaining the quality of their studies.

words.definitionEn: A careful examination to check condition, quality, or safety.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mechanic found a loose cable during the inspection.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular inspection of public buildings can identify structural problems before they become serious safety risks.

words.definitionEn: an official who checks that rules and standards are followed
words.exampleDailyEn: The inspector checked the kitchen before the restaurant opened.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A qualified building inspector can identify structural problems before they become serious risks to public safety.

words.definitionEn: Done by hand or operated by a person, not automatically.
words.exampleDailyEn: This manual coffee grinder takes some effort to turn.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although automation increases productivity, many industries still rely on manual labour for complex tasks.

words.definitionEn: to increase something as much as possible or use it fully
words.exampleDailyEn: We added shelves to maximize space in our tiny kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cities should improve public transport to maximize access to employment while reducing dependence on private cars.

words.definitionEn: Continuing to happen or develop, rather than being finished.
words.exampleDailyEn: The ongoing repairs mean we cannot use the kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Ongoing research into renewable energy is essential for reducing dependence on fossil fuels and limiting environmental damage.

words.definitionEn: something considered more important than other things
words.exampleDailyEn: Finding a warm home is our main priority now.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should give priority to preventive healthcare rather than focus exclusively on treating existing illnesses.

words.definitionEn: an established series of actions for completing a task
words.exampleDailyEn: The receptionist explained the procedure for joining the gym.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Every laboratory should establish a clear procedure for handling chemicals safely and disposing of waste responsibly.

words.definitionEn: To move or change position, direction, or focus.
words.exampleDailyEn: We shifted the sofa closer to the window.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should shift investment towards public transport to reduce traffic congestion and urban air pollution.

words.definitionEn: Accept responsibility for a task and begin doing it
words.exampleDailyEn: We undertook the repairs ourselves to save money.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should undertake further research before recommending major changes to national education policy.

words.definitionEn: Someone competing for a job or an elected position.
words.exampleDailyEn: Each candidate waited outside the office before their interview.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employers should assess each candidate fairly rather than rely on assumptions about their educational or cultural background.

words.definitionEn: Having enough skill and knowledge to do something well.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our new mechanic is competent and explains every repair clearly.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools need competent teachers who can adapt their methods to students with different learning needs.

words.definitionEn: The latest time by which something must be completed
words.exampleDailyEn: I stayed up late to meet the application deadline.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Setting a realistic deadline allows researchers to maintain quality without delaying the publication of important findings.

words.definitionEn: to say words aloud for someone or something to record
words.exampleDailyEn: Please dictate your message slowly while I write it down.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Financial pressures often dictate which courses universities offer, potentially limiting opportunities in less profitable subjects.

words.definitionEn: The main place from which an organisation is directed.
words.exampleDailyEn: She works at the company's headquarters near the river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Moving corporate headquarters to smaller cities can create jobs and reduce pressure on major urban centres.

words.definitionEn: achieving a lot or producing useful results
words.exampleDailyEn: I had a productive morning and finished my report.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Flexible working arrangements can help employees remain productive while balancing professional responsibilities with family commitments.

words.definitionEn: a subject or activity someone has particular knowledge or skill in
words.exampleDailyEn: Baking fruit pies has always been my grandmother's specialty.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Choosing a medical specialty requires students to consider their interests alongside the healthcare needs of the wider population.

words.definitionEn: Better in quality or performance than another
words.exampleDailyEn: These boots offer superior grip on wet paths.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public transport can provide a superior alternative to private cars when services are frequent and reliable.

words.definitionEn: to stop happening or doing something
words.exampleDailyEn: The bells finally ceased ringing just before midnight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Factories should cease discharging untreated wastewater into rivers to protect aquatic ecosystems and safeguard public health.

words.definitionEn: to begin something or start happening
words.exampleDailyEn: The evening concert will commence after a short welcome.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Construction of the new railway will commence once the environmental assessment has been completed.

words.definitionEn: Discuss something with others before making a decision.
words.exampleDailyEn: The coaches conferred quietly before choosing the final team.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities often confer honorary degrees on individuals who have made outstanding contributions to science or public service.

words.definitionEn: make an action or process easier
words.exampleDailyEn: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.

words.definitionEn: To cause a process or activity to begin.
words.exampleDailyEn: Someone needs to initiate a conversation about the noise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should initiate programmes that encourage residents to recycle household waste more effectively.

words.definitionEn: To end something, or to come to an end.
words.exampleDailyEn: We decided to terminate our gym membership last month.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employers should not terminate contracts without providing clear reasons and allowing workers sufficient time to respond.

words.definitionEn: A task or project, especially one requiring considerable effort.
words.exampleDailyEn: Renovating this old house is a much bigger undertaking.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Building a nationwide railway network is a major undertaking that requires sustained investment and careful planning.

words.definitionEn: to use something effectively for a particular purpose
words.exampleDailyEn: We utilise the spare room as a small office.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cities can utilise empty buildings to provide affordable housing and reduce pressure on surrounding farmland.

words.definitionEn: Happening or existing at the same time
words.exampleDailyEn: Two concurrent meetings meant I had to choose one.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Concurrent improvements in housing and public transport can make urban development more inclusive and sustainable.

words.definitionEn: Written communication between people, or the messages they exchange.
words.exampleDailyEn: She keeps her correspondence with her cousin in a drawer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Historical correspondence can reveal how ordinary families experienced social changes that official records describe only briefly.

words.definitionEn: A system arranging people or things by rank or importance
words.exampleDailyEn: There is a clear hierarchy among the restaurant staff.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A rigid workplace hierarchy may discourage junior employees from sharing ideas that could improve organisational performance.

words.definitionEn: training or formal introduction when someone joins an organisation
words.exampleDailyEn: Our induction included a tour of the whole office.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A structured induction programme can help new employees understand workplace expectations and adapt to their roles.

words.definitionEn: someone who works in a profession, especially medicine
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse suggested speaking to a qualified medical practitioner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Experienced practitioners should help design training programmes so that graduates develop skills relevant to their profession.

words.definitionEn: the act of keeping something or preventing someone from leaving
words.exampleDailyEn: Our manager improved staff retention by offering flexible hours.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular revision and adequate sleep can improve the retention of information among students preparing for examinations.

words.definitionEn: relating to plans for achieving important long-term goals
words.exampleDailyEn: We made a strategic decision to save before moving.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strategic investment in public transport can reduce congestion and support economic growth over the long term.

words.definitionEn: Lower in rank, authority, or importance.
words.exampleDailyEn: She accepted a subordinate role on the project.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In effective organisations, subordinate staff should feel comfortable raising concerns with senior managers without fear.

words.definitionEn: Someone who takes over another person's job or position.
words.exampleDailyEn: The retiring coach introduced her successor to the team.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A new leader should give their successor enough guidance to ensure that essential public services continue smoothly.

words.definitionEn: able to be moved or passed to another person or place
words.exampleDailyEn: These tickets are transferable, so your sister can use mine.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should help students develop transferable skills that remain valuable across different industries and careers.

words.definitionEn: a person who takes part in a competition
words.exampleDailyEn: Each entrant brought a homemade cake to the competition.
words.exampleIeltsEn: New entrants to the renewable energy market often struggle to compete with established companies for investment.

words.definitionEn: Combine or join together to form a single whole.
words.exampleDailyEn: The two narrow paths merge just beyond the bridge.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Small businesses may merge to reduce operating costs and compete more effectively with larger companies.

words.definitionEn: the act of carrying out a plan, order, or task
words.exampleDailyEn: The picnic plan was simple, but its execution proved tricky.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Successful execution of environmental policies requires adequate funding, clear responsibilities, and consistent monitoring by public authorities.

words.definitionEn: a collection of work showing someone's skills and experience
words.exampleDailyEn: She brought her photography portfolio to the interview.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A diversified investment portfolio can reduce financial risk, although it cannot guarantee steady returns.

words.definitionEn: Very skilled at doing something.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister is adept at fixing old bicycles.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers who are adept at using digital tools can adapt lessons to meet a wider range of learning needs.

words.definitionEn: To follow a rule, belief, or agreement closely.
words.exampleDailyEn: Everyone must adhere to the rules in this pool.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers must adhere to strict ethical standards when collecting personal information from participants in health studies.

words.definitionEn: Giving benefits or improving the chances of success
words.exampleDailyEn: Booking early was advantageous because we got cheaper tickets.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Flexible working arrangements can be advantageous to employers by improving staff satisfaction and reducing employee turnover.

words.definitionEn: a careful judgment of quality, performance, or a situation
words.exampleDailyEn: My manager praised my progress during today's performance appraisal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A thorough appraisal of environmental risks should take place before any major construction project begins.

words.definitionEn: to judge the quality, condition, or performance of something
words.exampleDailyEn: The coach appraised my technique and suggested some changes.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities must appraise the environmental impact of major construction projects before granting planning permission.

words.definitionEn: requiring considerable effort and sustained hard work
words.exampleDailyEn: The arduous climb left us exhausted but deeply satisfied.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Restoring damaged ecosystems is an arduous process that requires sustained investment and cooperation between scientists and local communities.

words.definitionEn: A strong hope or ambition to achieve something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her greatest aspiration is to open a small bakery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to affordable higher education can help young people fulfil their aspirations, regardless of their family income.

words.definitionEn: causing difficulty through excessive work, worry, or expense
words.exampleDailyEn: The extra paperwork became burdensome during our busiest week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Overly burdensome regulations may discourage small businesses from expanding, even when demand for their products is strong.

words.definitionEn: to confirm officially that something is true or meets standards
words.exampleDailyEn: An engineer certified that our new boiler was safe.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent organisations certify that certain products meet environmental standards, helping consumers make more informed purchasing decisions.

words.definitionEn: to praise someone or something, often publicly
words.exampleDailyEn: The coach commended Lina for helping her teammates.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Inspectors commended the school for providing additional support to students with different learning needs.

words.definitionEn: Careful to do duties thoroughly and correctly
words.exampleDailyEn: Our conscientious neighbour checks our plants every morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Conscientious employees contribute to workplace safety by following procedures carefully and reporting potential hazards promptly.

words.definitionEn: With care and a strong sense of responsibility.
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse conscientiously checked every item in the kit.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers who conscientiously review individual progress can identify learning difficulties before students fall significantly behind.

words.definitionEn: Familiar with a subject and able to discuss it
words.exampleDailyEn: Our new guide is conversant with the area's history.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Graduates entering the technology sector should be conversant with current debates about privacy and data protection.

words.definitionEn: A person or organisation responsible for protecting or managing something.
words.exampleDailyEn: The custodian carefully locked the cabinet containing ancient coins.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Museums act as custodians of cultural heritage, preserving valuable objects for research and future generations.

words.definitionEn: A situation where disagreement prevents any further progress.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our discussion reached a deadlock over who should pay.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An independent mediator may help break the deadlock when negotiations between employers and workers fail.

words.definitionEn: to send someone or something to a destination
words.exampleDailyEn: The shop will despatch your parcel tomorrow morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Emergency services must despatch rescue teams quickly when severe flooding isolates communities from essential supplies.

words.definitionEn: Working carefully and consistently with strong effort
words.exampleDailyEn: Our diligent neighbour checks her vegetable plants every morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Diligent research helps students develop stronger arguments and avoid relying on inaccurate information in academic essays.

words.definitionEn: An exact copy of something
words.exampleDailyEn: I keep a duplicate of the key at home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Research teams should share their findings to avoid duplicating work and wasting limited public funding.

words.definitionEn: To begin a project, activity, or course of action
words.exampleDailyEn: We are ready to embark on our kitchen renovation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Before students embark on professional training, they should consider both their interests and future employment opportunities.

words.definitionEn: Famous and respected for achievements in a particular field.
words.exampleDailyEn: An eminent surgeon visited our local hospital yesterday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities often invite eminent researchers to share their findings and inspire students to pursue academic careers.

words.definitionEn: To try hard to achieve something
words.exampleDailyEn: We endeavor to answer every message before dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should endeavor to make higher education accessible to students from a wider range of backgrounds.

words.definitionEn: To necessarily involve or require something
words.exampleDailyEn: This new job entails working some evenings and weekends.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Expanding public transport will entail substantial initial costs, although the environmental and social benefits may justify this investment.

words.definitionEn: Of excellent quality or exceptionally high ability.
words.exampleDailyEn: The small restaurant serves first-rate food at reasonable prices.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to first-rate training enables young workers to develop skills that employers increasingly value.

words.definitionEn: to make progress or an activity more difficult
words.exampleDailyEn: Heavy rain hampered our efforts to repair the fence.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Limited access to reliable internet services can hamper economic development in remote rural communities.

words.definitionEn: lift something heavy, often using ropes or machinery
words.exampleDailyEn: We hoisted the heavy suitcase onto the luggage rack.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Construction workers use specialised equipment to hoist heavy materials safely, reducing physical strain and workplace injuries.

words.definitionEn: The state of not working or doing anything.
words.exampleDailyEn: After weeks of idleness, I finally cleaned the garage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Long periods of enforced idleness during unemployment can damage confidence and make returning to work more difficult.

words.definitionEn: working hard and carefully over a sustained period
words.exampleDailyEn: My industrious neighbour grows vegetables and repairs furniture every weekend.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although industrious employees contribute greatly to productivity, employers must also provide adequate training and reasonable working conditions.

words.definitionEn: Intended to last until a permanent arrangement is made.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our interim manager will stay until we find a replacement.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The council introduced interim housing measures while permanent accommodation was being built for families displaced by flooding.
